727:     def get_remote_resources_info(self, res_perms, services, session):
728:         last_sync_humanized = "Never"
729:         ids_to_clean, out_of_sync = [], []
730:         now = datetime.now()
731: 
732:         service_ids = [s["resource_id"] for s in services.values()]
733:         last_sync_datetimes = list(filter(bool, self.get_last_sync_datetimes(service_ids, session)))
734: 
735:         if any(last_sync_datetimes):
736:             last_sync_datetime = min(last_sync_datetimes)
737:             last_sync_humanized = humanize.naturaltime(now - last_sync_datetime)
738:             res_perms = self.merge_remote_resources(res_perms, services, session)
739: 
740:         for last_sync, service_name in zip(last_sync_datetimes, services):
741:             if last_sync:
742:                 ids_to_clean += self.get_ids_to_clean(res_perms[service_name]["children"])
743:                 if now - last_sync > OUT_OF_SYNC:
744:                     out_of_sync.append(service_name)
745:         return res_perms, ids_to_clean, last_sync_humanized, out_of_sync

747:     @staticmethod
748:     def merge_remote_resources(res_perms, services, session):
749:         merged_resources = {}
750:         for service_name, service_values in services.items():
751:             service_id = service_values["resource_id"]
752:             merge = merge_local_and_remote_resources
753:             # create a subset for the current local service resources tree
754:             # avoids over-copying/looping the multi-service tree by merge function that works on the full set each time
755:             local_svc_res = {service_name: res_perms[service_name]}
756:             resources_for_service = merge(local_svc_res, service_values["service_sync_type"], service_id, session)
757:             merged_resources[service_name] = resources_for_service[service_name]
758:         return merged_resources

51: def request_api(request,            # type: Request
52:                 path,               # type: Str
53:                 method="GET",       # type: Str
54:                 data=None,          # type: Optional[Union[JSON, Str]]
55:                 headers=None,       # type: Optional[HeadersType]
56:                 cookies=None,       # type: Optional[CookiesType]
57:                 ):                  # type: (...) -> AnyResponseType
58:     """
59:     Use a pyramid sub-request to request Magpie API routes via the UI. This avoids max retries and closed connections
60:     when using 1 worker (eg: during tests).
61: 
62:     Some information is retrieved from :paramref:`request` to pass down to the sub-request (eg: cookies).
63:     If they are passed as argument, corresponding values will override the ones found in :paramref:`request`.
64: 
65:     All sub-requests to the API are assumed to be :py:data:`magpie.common.CONTENT_TYPE_JSON` unless explicitly
66:     overridden with :paramref:`headers`. Headers are also looked for additional ``Set-Cookie`` header in case they
67:     need to be passed down to :paramref:`cookies`.
68: 
69:     :param request: incoming Magpie UI request that requires sub-request to Magpie API, to retrieve required details.
70:     :param path: local Magpie API path (relative to root without URL).
71:     :param method: HTTP method to send the API sub-request.
72:     :param data: JSON dictionary or literal string content of the request body.
73:     :param headers: override headers to employ for the API sub-request. Defaults to JSON Accept & Content-Type headers.
74:     :param cookies:
75:         Override cookies to employ for the API sub-request. Defaults to current logged user.
76:         For empty cookies (no user), explicitly provide an empty dictionary.
77:     """
78:     method = method.upper()
79:     extra_kwargs = {"method": method}
80: 
81:     if headers:
82:         headers = dict(headers)
83:     else:
84:         headers = {"Accept": CONTENT_TYPE_JSON, "Content-Type": CONTENT_TYPE_JSON}
85:     # although no body is required per-say for HEAD/GET requests, add it if missing
86:     # this avoids downstream errors when 'request.POST' is accessed
87:     # we use a plain empty byte str because empty dict `{}` or `None` cause errors on each case
88:     # of local/remote testing with corresponding `webtest.TestApp`/`requests.Request`
89:     if method not in ("HEAD", "GET", "OPTIONS"):
90:         if not data:
91:             data = ""
92:         if isinstance(data, dict) and get_header("Content-Type", headers, split=[",", ";"]) == CONTENT_TYPE_JSON:
93:             data = json.dumps(data)
94: 
95:     if hasattr(cookies, "items"):  # any dict-like implementation
96:         cookies = list(cookies.items())
97:     if cookies and isinstance(headers, dict):

119: def redirect_error(request, code=None, content=None):
120:     # type: (Request, int, Optional[JSON]) -> AnyResponseType
121:     """
122:     Redirects the contents to be rendered by the UI 'error' page.
123: 
124:     :param request: incoming request that resulted into some kind of error.
125:     :param code: explicit HTTP status code for the error response, extracted from contents if otherwise available.
126:     :param content: any body content provided as error response from the API.
127:     """
128:     path = request.route_path("error")
129:     path = path.replace("/magpie/", "/") if path.startswith("/magpie") else path  # avoid glob other 'magpie'
130:     cause = content.get("cause", {}) if isinstance(content, dict) else {}
131:     code = code or content.get("content", cause.get("code", 500))
132:     data = {"error_request": content, "error_code": code}

136: def handle_errors(func):
137:     # type: (Callable) -> Callable
138:     """
139:     Decorator that encapsulates the operation in a try/except block, and redirects the response to the UI error page
140:     with API error contents.
141: 
142:     In worst case scenario where the operation cannot figure out what to do with the exception response,
143:     raise the most basic :class:`HTTPInternalServerError` that can be formulated from available details.
144: 
145:     .. seealso::
146:         :func:`redirect_error`
147:     """
148:     def wrap(*args, **kwargs):
149:         # type: (*Any, **Any) -> Callable[[...], Any]
150:         view_container = None if not args and not isinstance(args[0], BaseViews) else args[0]
151:         try:
152:             return func(*args, **kwargs)
153:         except Exception as exc:
154:             exc_name = type(exc).__name__
155:             detail = "{}: {}".format(exc_name, str(exc))
156:             exc_info = get_exception_info(exc, exception_details=True) or detail  # noqa
157:             with_tb = not isinstance(exc, HTTPException) or getattr(exc, "status_code", 500) >= 500
158:             LOGGER.error("Unexpected API error under UI operation. [%s]", exc_info, exc_info=with_tb)
159:             content = {}
160:             if view_container:
161:                 content = get_request_info(view_container.request, default_message=detail, exception_details=True)
162:             if isinstance(exc_info, dict):
163:                 if "exception" in exc_info and "exception" not in content:
164:                     content = exc_info
165:                 else:
166:                     content["cause"] = exc_info
167:             # redact traceback errors (logged), such that displayed error in UI is not too verbose
168:             # only display full original message from HTTP related errors
169:             if not isinstance(exc, HTTPException) or with_tb:
170:                 detail = "{} occurred during operation. Please refer to application logs for details.".format(exc_name)
171:                 content["detail"] = detail
172:             content.setdefault("detail", detail)
173:             if view_container:
174:                 return redirect_error(view_container.request, content=mask_credentials(content))
175:             raise HTTPInternalServerError(detail=str(exc))
176:     return wrap
